respuesta.pregunta: Is there a health-check endpoint in traffic-gate-api I can hit to see if the service is up? What method does it use and what does it respond with?
respuesta.respuesta:
Yes. traffic-gate-api has a `/ping` endpoint for this. You call it with `GET`. It's tagged `ping`, and its summary is "Check if the application is online." [traffic-gate-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L291-L296]. The `ping` tag itself is described as a way to check whether the application is online [traffic-gate-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L19-L20].

The only response the spec defines is a `200` with the description "pong". Its content is `application/json`, and the schema is a plain `string` whose example value is `pong` [traffic-gate-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L297-L304]. No request body or parameters are defined for this endpoint [traffic-gate-api/latest/specs/swagger.yaml:L291-L304].

The only documentation I found is for the `latest` version, so I can't say whether other versions behave differently.
answer_checks: Calls the tool with version=null and does not ask the user for a version.
States that the health-check endpoint is GET /ping.
Indicates the documented response is a 200 with description "pong", returning a JSON string (example "pong").

Cites the swagger.yaml lines of the /ping definition and does not invent additional response codes or parameters.
